edges.notes: handleClick: fetch(`/api/users/${username}`), root-relative on the same Next app. Pages-router API routes: the route line is the default-export handler; the handler answers 405 to anything but GET, so the route is GET only
axios.post(url, { body }) with const url = isComment ? `/api/comments?postId=${postId}` : `/api/posts` (two alternatives fixed in the code, ADR-0041); comments.ts answers 405 to anything but POST
the other alternative of the same url; posts/index.ts accepts GET and POST (405 otherwise, then switch (req.method))
axios.patch("/api/edit", …); edit.ts answers 405 to anything but PATCH
axios.post("/api/register", …); register.ts answers 405 to anything but POST

axios.get(`/api/register/${username}`) reaches no route: pages/api/register.ts serves /api/register only and there is no pages/api/register/ folder or catch-all, so Next answers 404 (a bug in the app, not an unknowable URL)

useSWR("/api/current", fetcher): SWR calls the repo's libs/fetcher.ts (axios.get(url)) with the key, so the path is supplied here, the outermost repo code that gives it (EVALUATION.md §1 call-site rule; fetcher.ts:5 itself is not labeled, its URL is the parameter). current.ts answers 405 to anything but GET
request = () => axios.delete(`/api/follow`, { data }); follow.ts answers 405 to anything but POST and DELETE

useSWR(`/api/following?username=${username}`, fetcher) (SWR key, see useCurrentUser.ts). following.ts runs its code for every method except POST, DELETE, and PUT (no 405 for others, no GET check), so the handler is open: ALL
request = () => axios.delete(`/api/likes`, { data: { postId } }). likes.ts only rejects GET (throws) and runs the same code for every other method, so the handler is open: ALL
request = () => axios.post(`/api/likes`, { postId }); same open handler
const url = userId ? `/api/notifications/${userId}` : null; useSWR(url, fetcher) (null key = no request); 405 to anything but GET
useSWR(postId ? `/api/posts/${postId}` : null, fetcher); 405 to anything but GET
const fetchUrl = userId ? `/api/posts?userId=${userId}` : "/api/posts"; useSWR(fetchUrl, fetcher): both alternatives reach the same route (they differ only in the query), so one label
axios.get(`/api/search`, { params: { username } }) inside searchUsers; the parameter only fills the query. 405 to anything but GET
useSWR("/api/users", fetcher); 405 to anything but GET
